title: Parliamentary vs Presidential System: Collective Responsibility, Cabinet Government & Shadow Cabinet

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: We adopted parliamentary democracy based on the British model, but how does our model differ from that model? 1. As regards legislation, the British Parliament is supreme or sovereign but in India, the power of the Parliament to legislate is limited. 2. In India, matters related to the constitutionality of the Amendment of an Act of the Parliament are referred to the Constitution Bench by the Supreme Court. Select the correct answer using the code given below.
relevant_prelims_pyqs.source_pdf: X-Factor Prelims- Indian Polity for Pre'2027.pdf

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: A Parliamentary System of Government is one in which

options.a: all political parties in the Parliament are represented in the Government
options.b: the Government is responsible to the Parliament and can be removed by it
options.c: the Government is elected by the people and can be removed by them
options.d: the Government is chosen by the Parliament but cannot be removed by it before completion of a fixed term

relevant_prelims_pyqs.source_pdf: X-Factor Prelims- Indian Polity for Pre'2027.pdf

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: Out of the following statements, choose the one that brings out the principle underlying the Cabinet form of Government :

options.a: An arrangement for minimizing the criticism against the Government whose responsibilities are complex and hard to carry out to the satisfaction of all.
options.b: A mechanism for speeding up the activities of the Government whose responsibilities are increasing day by day.
options.c: A mechanism of parliamentary democracy for ensuring collective responsibility of the Government to the people.
options.d: A device for strengthening the hands of the head of the Government whose hold over the people is in a state of decline.

relevant_prelims_pyqs.question_text: The main advantage of the parliamentary form of government is that

options.a: the executive and legislature work independently.
options.b: it provides continuity of policy and is more efficient.
options.c: the executive remains responsible to the legislature.
options.d: the head of the government cannot be changed without election.

options.a: Lok Sabha is elected directly by the people
options.d: Council of Ministers is responsible to the Lok Sabha

relevant_mains_pyqs.question_text: "The growth of cabinet system has practically resulted in the marginalisation of the parliamentary supremacy:" Elucidate. (10)
"The Attorney-General is the chief legal adviser and lawyer of the Government of India." Discuss. (15)

Indian Constitution has conferred the amending power on the ordinary legislative institutions with a few procedural hurdles. In view of this statement, examine the procedural and substantive limitations on the amending power of the Parliament to change the Constitution. (15)
Explain the structure of the Parliamentary Committee system. How far have the financial committees helped in the institutionalization of Indian Parliament? (15)
Discuss the role of Presiding Officers of state legislatures in maintaining order and impartiality in conducting legislative work and in facilitating best democratic practices. (10)
Discuss the role of the Vice -Presidents of India as the chairman of the Rajyasabha (10)
To what extent, in your view, the Parliament is able to ensure accountability of the executive in India? (10)

Do Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committees keep the administration on its toes and inspire reverence for parliamentary control? Evaluate the working of such committees with suitable examples. (15)
Explain the constitutional provisions under which Legislative Councils are established. Review the working and current status of Legislative Councils with suitable illustrations. (15)

"Once a speaker, Always a speaker'! Do you think the practice should be adopted to impart objectivity to the office of the Speaker of Lok Sabha? What could be its implications for the robust functioning of parliamentary business in India. (10)

Rajya Sabha has been transformed from a 'useless stepney tyre' to the most useful supporting organ in the past few decades. Highlight the factors as well as the areas in which this transformation could be visible. (15)
Individual Parliamentarian's role as the national lawmaker is on a decline, which in turn, has adversely impacted the quality of debates and their outcome. Discuss. (15)
Why do you think the committees are considered to be useful for parliamentary work? Discuss, in this context, the role of the Estimates Committee. (10)
